vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: dlazy-banana2
Version: 1.0.9

The skill is a wrapper for the dLazy CLI tool (@dlazy/cli) used for image generation and editing. It follows standard SaaS patterns, including local API key storage in ~/.dlazy/config.json and uploading local media to the service's endpoints (api.dlazy.com and files.dlazy.com) for processing. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration beyond the stated purpose, or harmful prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's behavior mostly matches an image-generation CLI, but the runtime instructions expect an API key and write a user config file even though no credentials or config paths are declared — this mismatch and the unreviewed npm package install are worth caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Nano Banana 2.0 image generation) align with the declared requirements: it expects npm/npx and points to an @dlazy/cli npm package and api.dlazy.com/files.dlazy.com endpoints — these are coherent for a CLI wrapper to a hosted image generation service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the dlazy CLI which will (a) send prompts to api.dlazy.com and (b) upload local files to files.dlazy.com. It also documents using the DLAZY_API_KEY environment variable and a CLI-auth command that writes ~/.dlazy/config.json. The skill instructions therefore read/use local file paths and environment/config secrets — this is expected for an image CLI but the skill's declared requirements did not advertise these env/config accesses, so the instructions access more sensitive state than declared.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only (no install spec in the registry), but metadata recommends installing or running a pinned npm package (@dlazy/cli@1.0.9) via npm or npx. Installing an npm CLI is a reasonable choice for this purpose, but npm packages have moderate risk if not reviewed. The metadata provides a GitHub repo and pinned version which helps auditing; using npx avoids persisting a global binary.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required env vars, yet SKILL.md explicitly references DLAZY_API_KEY and documents writing credentials to ~/.dlazy/config.json. This is a mismatch: the skill will require and persist a secret (API key) and read local files, but the skill did not declare those environment/config requirements up front. Declaring no required env vars despite needing an API key lowers transparency.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. It will cause the CLI (if installed) to store an API key in a user config file (~/.dlazy/config.json) under the user's account, which is normal for CLI tools and is documented in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to be a thin CLI client for the dLazy image-generation service and is mostly coherent with that purpose, but beware of two issues before installing or using it:

- API key & config persistence: The SKILL.md requires a DLAZY_API_KEY (or running dlazy auth set) and says the CLI stores the key in ~/.dlazy/config.json. Yet the registry lists no required environment variables or config paths. Expect the CLI to read/write that config file and to upload any local files you pass to files.dlazy.com. Only proceed if you trust dlazy.com and the package maintainer.

- Unreviewed npm package: The skill recommends installing @dlazy/cli@1.0.9 from npm. Prefer running with npx (npx @dlazy/cli@1.0.9) to avoid a global install. Before installing globally, review the GitHub repo and the exact package version (and ideally check release source or checksums) to ensure there is no unexpected behavior.

Recommendations:
- Ask the publisher to declare required env vars (DLAZY_API_KEY) and config path in the skill metadata so it's explicit.
- Inspect https://github.com/dlazyai/cli and the npm package @dlazy/cli@1.0.9 for any code that exfiltrates data beyond api.dlazy.com/files.dlazy.com.
- Use npx to avoid global installs and limit persistence. Keep API keys scoped, rotated, and revoke if suspicious activity appears.

What would change this assessment: If the registry metadata were corrected to declare the API key/config path and/or if you or the reviewer inspected the GitHub repo and confirmed the npm package only communicates with the documented endpoints, confidence would rise to high (benign). If the package or repo contained unexpected remote endpoints, obfuscated code, or code that reads unrelated local data, the verdict would be more severe.
